You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily ｜Trump Says US-Iran Negotiation Window Is Limited; Apple Overtakes Nvidia to Reclaim World’s Largest Market Cap; US Stocks Mixed as Storage and Optical Communications Come Under Pressure (July 28, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Developments
Trump Presses for Lower Rates; Citadel Securities Warns of Possible Surprise Hike
Trump said Fed Chair Warsh is excellent but rates should be lower, stating that the United States should have the lowest rates in the world and that costs are falling rapidly.
Citadel Securities expects a possible 25 bp rate hike this week to reinforce the Fed’s anti-inflation credibility and end excessive reliance on forward guidance.
Morgan Stanley data shows investors have increased dollar long positions ahead of the FOMC meeting.
Market Impact : Trump’s call for rate cuts coexists with hawkish hike warnings, heightening policy uncertainty, supporting the dollar in the near term and pressuring valuations of risk assets.
International Commodities
US-Iran Pause Drives Sharp Oil Price Decline
Trump decided to pause strikes on Iran to give negotiations another chance, while emphasizing that if diplomacy fails, he may order a return to strong military action, noting the window is “not long.”
Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu arrived in the United States and will meet Trump on the 28th, planning to present intelligence showing Iran is still advancing nuclear facilities and missile reconstruction.
Market Impact : Expectations of geopolitical de-escalation rapidly eroded the previous risk premium. Crude oil fell sharply, easing inflation concerns, though the risk of negotiation breakdown remains and market sentiment stays sensitive.
Macroeconomic Policy
Tariff Impact Limited; AI Review Framework Nears; CME Launches Single-Stock Futures
The USTR stated that the new Section 301 tariffs will not create additional economic impact beyond the current range and will cover the vast majority of imports.
The Trump administration is close to finalizing a voluntary AI review framework requiring frontier models to be submitted to the government before public release, with an August 1 deadline.
CME launched cash-settled single-stock futures on 55 US stocks plus micro contracts, supporting 23-hour trading (including SpaceX, Micron, etc.).
Market Impact : Policy clarity reduces trade uncertainty. The AI framework may affect model release timing, while single-stock futures expand leveraged trading windows.
II. Market Recap
Commodities FX Performance (Real-time Update)
Spot Gold : ~$4,052/oz, -0.61%
Spot Silver : ~$57.2/oz, -2.04%
WTI Crude : ~$81.6/bbl, -1.15%
Brent Crude : ~$81.35/bbl, +0.78%
US Dollar Index (DXY) : ~101.47, -0.05%
Driver Analysis : The pause in US-Iran strikes and renewed negotiation hopes quickly compressed the oil risk premium. Both WTI and Brent declined significantly, easing inflation concerns and supporting risk assets. Gold and silver came under mild pressure amid falling oil prices and a relatively firm dollar, with safe-haven demand cooling. The linkage is clear: geopolitical de-escalation → lower oil prices → cooler inflation expectations → renewed discussion of Fed policy space. However, Trump’s “limited window” comments keep markets cautious, and near-term commodity volatility will continue to track negotiation progress.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : ~$63,232, -2.82%
ETH : ~$1,875, -3.34%
Total Crypto Market Cap : ~$2.27 trillion, -1.5%
Liquidations (24h) : Total ~$677 million, of which longs ~$533 million
Bitget BTC/USDT Liquidation Map : Around the current price (~$63,162), long/short liquidation pressure is relatively light. Heavy high-leverage short liquidation clusters sit in the $64,400–$66,500 zone. A continued rise could trigger cascading short liquidations and amplify upside momentum. Cumulative long leverage below is notably smaller than short leverage above (~$190 million vs ~$620 million), indicating higher short-side risk concentration and greater probability of squeeze volatility on upside breaks than on downside moves.
Spot ETF Flows : BTC spot ETFs have shown mixed recent flows. Last Friday saw a single-day net outflow of $240 million; current 24h dynamic net outflow is about $2.8 million.
Driver Analysis : Falling oil prices and geopolitical de-escalation lifted risk appetite, allowing crypto to stabilize overall. ETH’s relative strength points to rotation into higher-beta assets. Liquidations were dominated by shorts, reflecting short covering support. ETF flows remain volatile, showing continued institutional caution. At the macro level, the approaching FOMC meeting and Trump’s rate-cut pressure form a key tension. Technically, BTC is holding key support. Near-term bias is range-bound to mildly constructive, with focus on negotiation progress and FOMC outcomes for liquidity impact.
US Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones : Closed at 52,210 (+0.51%), supported by lower oil prices boosting blue chips
SP 500 : Closed at 7,413 (+0.02%), barely ending a multi-session losing streak
Nasdaq : Closed at 24,932 (-0.18%), weighed by semiconductor weakness
Tech Giants Performance
NVDA : ~$196.5, -4.99%
AAPL : ~$336.9, +1.17%
MSFT : ~$389, +1.94%
[...]
GOOGL : ~$326.6, +2.13%
[...]
AMZN : ~$231.4, -0.31%
[...]
META : ~$593.9, -0.22%
[...]
TSLA : ~$309.2, -1.22%
[...]
Performance Summary Driver Analysis : Tech showed clear internal divergence. Apple’s steady performance allowed it to overtake Nvidia as the world’s largest company by market cap, while Microsoft and Google also strengthened. Nvidia fell sharply on concerns over AI infrastructure costs and competition, dragging the Nasdaq. AI application software names (Shopify, Palantir, etc.) remained strong, indicating preference for monetization over pure hardware narratives. The overall tone was supported by oil price relief, but semiconductor and storage weakness reflected reassessment of capital spending and supply-demand dynamics. Drivers are highly stock-specific rather than uniform.
[...]
Event Overview : AMD declined 5.17% to $494.95, joining Nvidia in weighing on semiconductors and the Nasdaq. Market Interpretation : Uncertainty around the return cycle of AI infrastructure spending is being re-priced. Optimistic assumptions about future hyperscaler capex growth have moderated. As a key GPU and data-center chip participant, AMD was directly affected. The structural split between hardware pressure and software strength became more pronounced. Investment Implication : The long-term AI compute demand thesis remains intact, but near-term valuation and spending pace require stricter validation. Volatility may stay higher than that of application software names.
[...]
6. Apple (AAPL) – Reclaims World’s Largest Market Cap
[...]
Event Overview : Apple’s market cap rose to approximately $4.95 trillion, surpassing Nvidia’s roughly $4.77 trillion—the first time since April 2025 that Apple has reclaimed the global No. 1 ranking. Shares rose about 1.17% to $336.91. The company reports earnings later this week. Market Interpretation : Amid heightened volatility in the AI narrative, investors are once again assigning a higher premium to companies with robust free cash flow and steady services growth. The Apple–Nvidia market-cap switch essentially reflects a rebalancing from “high growth but high uncertainty” toward “certainty and earnings quality.” Investment Implication : The rotation signals a phase shift in risk appetite. Apple’s upcoming results will be a key test of consumer electronics and services growth resilience.
[...]
7. Nvidia (NVDA) – AI Infrastructure Cost Concerns Trigger Sell-Off
[...]
According to ARK Invest’s website, Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest bought 124,543 shares of SpaceX (SPCX) on Monday, valued at approximately $14.14 million, and 27,864 shares of Tesla (TSLA), valued at about $8.62 million.
